hints: First count all sequences without the requirement.
Subtract sequences missing at least one value, while correcting overlaps.
Use inclusion-exclusion over the set of missing values.
analogy: Mark forbidden labels and alternate subtraction and addition as overlapping restrictions are counted.
example: For n=3 and k=2, there are 2^3 sequences; subtract the two constant sequences to get 6.
algorithm: Compute the sum over j=0..k of (-1)^j * C(k,j) * (k-j)^n modulo 1000000007. Precompute factorials and inverse factorials to obtain binomial coefficients, and compute each power by binary exponentiation. Normalize negative results modulo the prime.
correctness: For any sequence missing r labels, its total coefficient is the alternating sum of C(r,j), which is zero if r>0 and one if r=0. Therefore only sequences containing every label remain.
complexity: For length n and alphabet size k, time is O(k log n+k) and space O(k).
